local_checks.result: safeFetchHtml (safe-fetch.ts:221-240) uses one AbortController for all hops. Its signal is passed to every http(s).request (line 163). local_checks.invariant: Shop HTTP requests holding a Limiter slot must have a deadline and a body cap
local_checks.result: Http.follow calls fetch with no AbortSignal or timeout (http.ts:84) and buffers the whole body with res.text() and no cap (http.ts:96). It follows up to 10 redirects to any host (http.ts:87-94). GET retries are bounded to 3 with exponential backoff and jitter (http.ts:58-66), so there is no retry storm. Limiter (limiter.ts:2-21) releases in finally, so a rejected task frees its slot, but a never-settling fetch holds a slot indefinitely. Only undici's library defaults apply (headers timeout; the body timeout is per-chunk idle, so a slow drip is unbounded); these are dependency facts, not repo-visible. Minor non-security quirk: a new caller arriving between release and the woken waiter's resume can push active above max.

local_checks.invariant: A lower-trust principal must not be able to hold cartLock/Limiter or stall the bot's update loop
local_checks.result: cartLock (Mutex, limiter.ts:30-42) has no timeout. A hung request inside add/setQuantity/clearCart/prepareOrder/confirmOrder (cart.ts:70,123,138; checkout.ts:134,162) blocks every later cart and checkout task until restart. The bot awaits work() inside handlers under grammy long polling (bot.ts:76-87, 670), so one stalled shop request also delays later updates. A stalled daily job never re-arms scheduleDaily (bot.ts:645-655). Every URL reaching Http is a fixed shop path or comes from a shop response (all call sites enumerated). Recipe links use safeFetchHtml with its own 10 s/2 MB limits, not Http; Telegram text reaches Http only as URL-encoded search parameters (products.ts:48-52). Only Mercator, a host it redirects to, or a network failure can cause the stall. That is the same principal that can already deny service, and the effect is limited to the owner's own single-user process. No lower-trust input-to-cost path exists, so this is hardening.
